newsitem.title: USA: Holocaust victims sue European insurers.
newsitem.headline: Holocaust victims sue European insurers.

text.p: Holocaust victims and their families sued a group of European insurance companies on Monday alleging the companies withheld, concealed or converted the cash value and proceeds of policies sold before 1946.

The suit, filed in Manhattan federal court, seeks class action certification. The proposed class consists of individuals who between 1920 and 1945 bought life, property and casualty insurance policies and annuities from the defendants.
The suit estimates that the class would exceed 10,000 members. It seeks billions of dollars in damages to be determined at trial.

The defendants in the case are: Assicurazioni Generali S.p.A. of Trieste, Italy; Wiener Allianz Verischerungs Aktiengesellschaft of Vienna; A.G.F. Assurances Generales de France Vie of Paris; Riunione Adriatica Di Sicurta S.p.A. of Milan; Allianz Group of Germany of Munich; Der Anker Allgemeine Versicherungs AG of Vienna; and Bavarian Reinsurance Co of Munich.
The suit alleges that the companies do extensive business in the United States and some have agency agreements with U.S. insurance companies including Aetna Life Insurance & Casualty Co.

According to the suit, the defendants "with a reputation for confidentiality and professionalism" encouraged European citizens who were fearful of Nazi persecution to deposit their assets with and to purchase insurance to safeguard their family's futures.
Members of the class who were unable to flee the persecution were arrested and their assets, including the insurance policies and numbers, were taken by the Nazis, the suit alleged.
The policies were then improperly transferred, liquidated or cashed in, the suit alleged.
"In many instances proceeds from the insurance policies of Holocaust victims were used to finance and extend the war or enrich Nazi war criminals," plaintiffs alleged.

The plaintiffs accuse the insurers of hiding vital information and allege that they falsely stated they had conducted exhaustive searches and found no proceeds of accumulated cash value or any other policy benefits.
